description: PLC-03's firing-arc probe. Not validated by tools/validate/validate_data.py -- it lives under data/schema/, which discover_documents() excludes, the same way the schema files and the TER-02/TER-08 fixtures are excluded. That is the whole reason the probe TOWER ROW lives here rather than in data/towers.json: the issue asks for a throwaway 60-degree weapon driven through both engines, and no shipped row may gain `cos_half_angle` or the arc path stops being provably inert. tools/arc_parity.py drives sim/engine.py over this document; scripts/test/arc_parity.gd drives scripts/anchor_sim.gd over the identical document; the two fire patterns are diffed tick for tick, and each is also checked against the analytic window below, which is derived from the geometry rather than from either implementation.

towers.name: Probe Cone
towers.note: cos 30 degrees -- a 60-degree cone pointing +y, straight at the lane. Range 6.0 reaches 5.657 tiles of lane either side of the emplacement; the cone reaches 1.155. The arc is what decides, not the range, which is the entire point of the fixture.

towers.name: Probe Cone, unnormalised
towers.note: The same cone with a facing three times as long. |facing|^2 is folded into the right-hand side of the test rather than divided out by normalising, so this must produce a window of the identical WIDTH as arc-probe-cone, just centred on its own position. If anyone 'simplifies' the test to assume a unit vector, this row is the one that goes red.

towers.name: Probe Half-plane
towers.note: cos_half_angle 0 is a half-angle of exactly 90 degrees, so the squared compare `dot*dot >= 0 * d2` is vacuously true and the ONLY thing deciding this row is the `dot >= 0` sign guard. It fires down-lane and never up-lane. Delete the sign guard and this row's window doubles: it is the fixture's whole defence of the guard the squared form makes necessary.

towers.name: Probe Omni
towers.note: The control: identical stats, no `cos_half_angle` and no `facing` at all. Proves the absent-key path is the omnidirectional one, and gives the arc'd rows something to be strictly narrower than -- an arc test that silently never engaged would make every row's window look like this one's.

enemies.name: Probe Walker
enemies.note: A million hit points on purpose: it must survive every shot and walk the whole lane, so the fire pattern is a statement about the ARC and never about a kill. Speed 2.0 at DT=1/30 covers 0.0667 tiles per tick, so 280 ticks walks 18.67 of the lane's 19 tiles and it never leaks either.

expected.note: dot = 2 (the 2-tile standoff), gate = cos^2 * |facing|^2 = 0.75. In arc when 4 >= 0.75 * (dx^2 + 4), i.e. dx^2 <= 4/3, i.e. |dx| <= 1.1547005383792515 about x=9.5. Derived from the geometry, not read off either engine.
The same +-1.1547005383792515 half-width about x=15.0. Identical width to build 0 despite |facing| = 3 -- that equality is the claim.

The half-plane: everything from its own x onward that is also inside range 6.0 of (4, 2), which is x <= 9.657. The lower bound is the sign guard and it is the bound under test; the upper is just the range circle, so the window is stated as the half-plane and the shot count carries the rest.
No arc: purely the range circle, x = 9.5 +- sqrt(6^2 - 4^2) = 9.5 +- 5.656854249492381. The standoff here is 4.0 tiles, not 2.0, because the control sits on the far side of the lane at y=6.
